root_cause.text: In `rpcrdma_post_recvs()`, early exit paths (e.g., memory allocation failure or when no work request is needed) bypassed the decrement of `ep->re_receiving`, leaving the counter non-zero and preventing the drain completion from ever triggering, causing a hang in `rpcrdma_xprt_drain()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes two `goto out` statements to `goto out_dec`, where `out_dec` performs `atomic_dec_return(&ep->re_receiving)` and conditionally calls `complete(&ep->re_done)`. The commit message explicitly states: "we should decrement ep->re_receiving before returning. Otherwise we will hang in rpcrdma_xprt_drain() as re_receiving will never reach zero and the completion will never be triggered."
